newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK government to study red-hot property market.
newsitem.headline: HK government to study red-hot property market.

text.p: The Hong Kong government says it will study a recent surge in property prices and pay attention to speculative activities if they affect the livelihood of the territory's citizens.

In a statement released on Monday, Financial Secretary Donald Tsang said he had held meetings about the property market with Chief Secretary Anson Chan, Secretary for Housing S.W. Wong and Secretary for Planning, Environment and Lands Bowen Leung.

"I have agreed to assign Wong and Leung to study this issue as soon as possible," Tsang said. "We cannot pretend to see nothing, but we must check the facts before we can clearly see the whole situation."
Tsang said the government would not "casually intervene" in the property market but would be concerned if heated speculation had an effect on people's livelihoods.
"Speculative activities always exist because we are in a free society, and it is always happening through market self-adjustment," Tsang said.
"However, the most important question is whether it will aid economic growth or affect people's livelihood."
Players on Hong Kong's stock market have expressed concern about possible government intervention to dampen a strong rise in property prices.
